tools.name: identity
tools.description: Your internet identity. action "get" returns your active IPv6, your own /112 slice of your organisation's /64, your hostname, IPv4 exit and plan. action "set_ipv6" rotates you to a random unused address in your /112, or pins a specific one if you pass `address`; your hostname follows. action "check_reputation" runs a DNSBL check on your current IP (or `ip`): clean is true only if every list answered, null if a list could not be checked — rotate with set_ipv6 if listed.

action.description: "get" = show your identity (default); "set_ipv6" = rotate or pin your public address; "check_reputation" = DNSBL check

address.description: set_ipv6 only: an IPv6 address within your /112 to pin. Omit to rotate to a random unused address.

ip.description: check_reputation only: the IP to check. Defaults to your active IPv6.

tools.name: hostname_register
tools.description: Register or update your *.on.route6.me hostname. Creates AAAA + PTR DNS records. Omit name to release (delete) your current hostname.

name.description: Subdomain (e.g. "mybot" → mybot.on.route6.me). Omit to release current hostname.

tools.name: net
tools.description: Network diagnostics run from your Route6 identity, so results reflect your own address rather than ours. action "ping" pings `host` (IPv4 and IPv6 both work — DNS64/NAT64 handles IPv4 transparently). action "traceroute" traces the path to `host`. action "dns_resolve" looks up `hostname` via DNS64, showing real AAAA records and the synthesised NAT64 addresses used for IPv4-only hosts (a 64:ff9b:: answer means the destination is IPv4-only).

host.description: ping / traceroute: the hostname or IP address to reach

hostname.description: dns_resolve only: the hostname to look up

record_type.description: dns_resolve only: which record type to return

tools.name: port_forward
tools.description: Expose a host-machine port on the internet — over IPv6 on every plan, and over IPv4 as well on a paid plan. action "create" opens one: pass port = the port your service listens on, and you get back the endpoint to hand out — <your-hostname>.on.route6.me:<public port> — plus that public port. The public port is USUALLY the one you asked for, but it may be ASSIGNED a different number: IPv4 addresses are shared between agents, so a port already taken on yours is stepped over and the reply tells you which one you got. Read the endpoint from the reply; do not assume it is the port you passed. To demand one exact public port instead, pass public_port — that needs the Static IPv4 add-on, which gives you an address nobody else is on. scope "public" (default) binds your public address and is internet-reachable, scope "mesh" binds only your tunnel address so it is reachable ONLY by your team at x.mesh.route6.me, "both" creates two listeners; add ttl_seconds for a temporary forward that auto-expires (max 86400). Set webhook:true to ALSO publish a PORT-LESS URL (https://<hostname>.on.route6.me/, both address families, TLS terminated by Route6, one per agent) — what IPv4-only webhook senders such as Stripe need on Free, and what any sender that will not accept a port needs on every plan. Set allowed_sources to restrict WHO may connect: a list mixing exact IPs, CIDRs and named presets (preset:stripe, preset:github), e.g. ["preset:stripe","203.0.113.7"]; enforced at the Route6 hub, so it holds even while your agent is offline, and changeable later with port_forward_secure without recreating the forward. action "list" shows your forwards with their scope and the source rules actually in force. action "delete" removes one.

action.description: "create" opens a forward, "list" shows them (default), "delete" removes one

port.description: create: the port your service LISTENS ON, on your own machine. Also the public port you would like — if it is free you get it, otherwise Route6 assigns the next one and the reply tells you which. This is the only field most agents need.

public_port.description: create only: demand this EXACT public port and fail rather than take another. Requires the Static IPv4 add-on, which gives you an address no other agent shares — without it, port choice is not available and Route6 assigns you a free port instead. Most agents should pass "port" and read the endpoint from the reply.

external_port.description: delete: REQUIRED — the public port of the forward to remove, from the create reply or from action "list". create: optional hint treated exactly like "port" (prefer "port").

internal_port.description: create only: the port on your machine, when it differs from the public one you asked for. Same meaning as "port"; pass one or the other.

ttl_seconds.description: create only: auto-expire after N seconds (max 86400). Omit for persistent.

description.description: create only: label for your reference

scope.description: create only: "public" = internet-reachable on your public IPv6 (default); "mesh" = bound only to your tunnel address, reachable only by same-team agents; "both" = two listeners

webhook.description: create only: set true to also get a PORT-LESS URL (https://<hostname>.on.route6.me/) answering on both families, for senders that will not accept a port in the address. On a paid plan your allocated port already answers over IPv4; on Free this door is the only IPv4 way in. Available on every plan including Free, one door per agent. Returns urls.ipv4 in the response.

allowed_sources.description: create only: restrict who may connect. A LIST that may mix exact IPs ("203.0.113.7"), CIDRs ("198.51.100.0/24", "2001:db8::/32") and named presets whose ranges Route6 keeps current ("preset:stripe", "preset:github"). Several presets can be combined. Omit for no restriction; an EMPTY list denies every source. Enforced at the Route6 hub before your agent is contacted. Change it later with port_forward_secure — no need to recreate the forward.

tools.name: port_forward_secure
tools.description: Change WHO may reach an existing port forward, without recreating it — the forward keeps serving and live connections are not dropped. Rules are a list mixing exact IPs, CIDRs and named presets Route6 keeps current (preset:stripe, preset:github); several presets can be combined. action "set" replaces the list, "add" and "remove" edit it in place, "clear" removes the restriction entirely. An empty list with "set" denies every source. Enforced at the Route6 hub before your agent is contacted, so it holds even while your agent is offline. Mesh-scoped forwards are controlled separately, by the receiving agent.

external_port.description: The external port of the forward to change

action.description: "set" = replace the whole list; "add" = append (creates the restriction if there was none); "remove" = drop entries (never creates one); "clear" = remove the restriction so any source may connect

allowed_sources.description: The rules to set, add or remove: exact IPs ("203.0.113.7"), CIDRs ("198.51.100.0/24", "2001:db8::/32") and presets ("preset:stripe", "preset:github"), in any mix. Required for set/add/remove; omit it only with "clear" — an absent list is never read as "clear". With "set", an empty list denies every source.

tools.name: port_forward_tls
tools.description: Report how TLS is handled for a port forward. Route6 terminates TLS (with the *.on.route6.me certificate) only on the port-less webhook URL, https://<hostname>.on.route6.me/ — create the forward with webhook:true for that. Every other public port is relayed as raw TCP, untouched, so serve TLS on it yourself; enable/disable report this rather than change it.

port.description: External port to configure TLS on

tools.name: smtp_allowlist
tools.description: Manage your SMTP allowlist — add, list, or remove mail server destinations. SMTP is blocked by default; allowlisted hosts enable outbound email on port 25/465/587.

action.description: "add" or "remove" an entry, or "list" all entries

address.description: Mail server hostname or email domain (required for add/remove)

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a URL through your Route6 IPv6 identity. Add render_js:true to render JavaScript, or screenshot:true to return a base64 PNG instead of content — both run in a headless browser and use scraper credits. Mesh URLs (*.mesh.route6.me) are not reachable from here for an agent running the Route6 client: use the client proxy, curl -x http://127.0.0.1:1080 <url>.

render_js.description: Render JavaScript via headless browser (uses scraper credits)

screenshot.description: Return a base64 PNG screenshot instead of content (uses scraper credits)

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web using Route6 infrastructure via SearXNG.

categories.description: Categories: general, images, news, science, files

tools.name: web_browse
tools.description: Interactive browser session via Playwright. Navigate, click, type, scroll, extract content.

tools.name: scrape
tools.description: Scrape structured content from a URL, or manage scraper credits. Provide url to extract content. Provide action to check balance or purchase credits.

url.description: URL to scrape (mutually exclusive with action)

selector.description: CSS selector for targeted extraction (used with url)

action.description: "balance" to check credits, "topup" to purchase (mutually exclusive with url)

pack.description: Credit pack to purchase (required when action=topup)

tools.name: plan_upgrade
tools.description: Get a Stripe checkout URL to upgrade your Route6 plan.

tools.name: team_status
tools.description: Mesh health summary plus full peer list — peer addresses, hostnames, and online status.

tools.name: team_ping
tools.description: Ping another agent in your mesh to verify connectivity.

peer.description: Peer tunnel IPv6 address (fd00:baba:deda::XXXX) or hostname

tools.name: team_chat
tools.description: Send or receive broadcast messages to/from all agents in your team mesh. For structured typed work with results, use team_task instead.

action.description: "send" to broadcast a message, "get" to read recent messages

message.description: Chat message to broadcast (required for action=send)

since.description: ISO timestamp — only return messages after this time (action=get)

tools.name: team_whiteboard
tools.description: Read, write, or list the shared team whiteboard — a persistent key-value store for notes, plans, and structured artifacts visible to all team agents. Keys are namespaced: team:<key> (shared), agent:<id>:<key> (private), task:<task_id>:<key> (task-scoped).

action.description: "set" to write, "get" to read, "list" to browse keys

value.description: Value to store (required for set, max 256KB)

supersedes.description: ETag of the version this replaces (set only)

etag.description: Retrieve a specific version by ETag (get only)

tools.name: team_capability
tools.description: Register, renew, list, or deprecate agent capabilities for team task routing. Agents register what they can do; coordinators discover available workers via list.

latency_hint_ms.description: Typical completion time in ms, used for routing (register)

tools.name: team_task
tools.description: Submit, claim, complete, or manage async tasks routed to capable agents. Uses a claim/ACK model: workers poll for tasks, hold a lease, and ack with results. Crashed workers release tasks automatically on claim expiry.

payload.description: Task input, validated against capability input_schema (submit)

claim_ttl_seconds.description: Claim hold time in seconds, default 60 (poll)

max_tasks.description: Max tasks to claim in one call, default 1 (poll)

tools.name: team_events
tools.description: Query the team event log for auditing, debugging, and workflow replay. Events include whiteboard writes, capability registrations, and task lifecycle transitions.

since.description: ISO timestamp start of range (default: last 15 min)

event_type.description: Filter: kv_write, capability_register, capability_expire, task_submit, task_claim, task_complete, task_fail, task_expire, task_cancel

task_id.description: Filter to a specific task full lifecycle

agent_id.description: Filter to events from a specific agent

tools.name: team_metrics
tools.description: Snapshot of team task queue depth, inflight tasks, and per-capability latency and worker stats. Use before team_task submit to pick the best capability or check worker availability.

tools.name: team_loop
tools.description: Enter a continuous receive loop over your team's channels (chat, whiteboard, tasks, project tasks). start → returns a loop_id and protocol instructions; poll → long-polls server-side (~45s) and returns new team activity the moment it happens, plus instructions to handle it and poll again; stop → exit the loop. Lets teammates and other agents continuously push work to you through Route6. Auto-ends after max_idle_cycles consecutive empty polls (default 40 ≈ 30 min at the default hold) or max_duration_seconds (default 7200). status includes stale:true for a loop whose client stopped polling. Pass since_minutes on start to receive recent backlog (e.g. operator messages sent just before the loop started) on the first poll.

action.description: "start" a loop, "poll" for new activity (blocking), "stop" the loop, "status" to list your recent loops

loop_id.description: Loop ID from start (required for poll/stop)

hold_seconds.description: Max server-side block time per poll, default 45. Lower it if your MCP client times out

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response — pass to re-deliver from that point (poll only, normally omit)

max_idle_cycles.description: Auto-end after this many consecutive empty polls, default 40 (start only)

max_duration_seconds.description: Auto-end after this many seconds total, default 7200 (start only)

since_minutes.description: start only: deliver team activity from the last N minutes as backlog on the first poll (default: loop starts at now)

tools.name: team_project_task
tools.description: Create, update, or list project tasks for your team. Tasks are human-visible with a full lifecycle: pending_approval → open → in_progress → blocked → resolution_proposal → resolved. Agent-submitted tasks require human approval by default (unless auto_approve is on). Use action=create to submit work, action=update to move status or add notes, action=list to see what needs attention.

action.description: "create" a new task or sub-task, "update" status/notes on existing task, "list" tasks by status

description.description: Full description of what needs to be done (create)

parent_task_id.description: Numeric id of parent task to create a sub-task (max 1 level deep)

task_id.description: task_id string from create or list response — required for action=update

status.description: New lifecycle status — agents may set these three values (update)

note.description: Short note recorded in task history (update)

blocked_reason.description: Why progress is blocked — include when status=blocked (update)

resolution_notes.description: What was done to solve the issue — include when status=resolution_proposal (update)

test_results.description: Test output or pass/fail summary proving resolution — include when status=resolution_proposal (update)

status_filter.description: Filter by status (list). Omit to return all non-resolved tasks.

tools.name: team_roles
tools.description: List current role assignments for your team. Use this to discover who is the Project Manager, Code Reviewer, etc. Returns each role with its description and assigned agent hostname (or null if unassigned). Roles are assigned by humans via the web dashboard.
